column1: Edwin/s0|Does she escape often?|Only as far as the feed bucket. She has ambitions, but they are quite local.|Could I help count?|Gladly. Keep an eye on the one pretending to sleep.
Edwin/s1|Do you help at the mill?|When they need another pair of hands. Nobody here gets to have just one job.|Is the coop finished?|Ask the hens. They keep making suggestions with their beaks.

Edwin/w0|Have you tried refusing?|A hungry winter is a poor time to gamble with men carrying swords.|Does he leave enough?|Some years. We share what we can when a neighbour comes up short.|Can anyone object?|Hettie does. The rest of us stand beside her.

Edwin/w1|Do the hens know?|They have noticed the larger breakfast. Politics can wait.|What will you do first?|Repair the grain store before the rain comes. Freedom still needs a sound roof.|Will there be a feast?|If somebody else does the cooking. I can supply eggs.

Edwin/e0|Was the grain spoiled?|Some of it. I should have raised the bin sooner, but a mistake is useful if you remember it.|Can I help with the bin?|Check the lid after you collect the eggs. A small job done regularly saves a large one.
Edwin/e1|Who needs help now?|Hettie will know. She notices an empty cupboard before its owner thinks to ask.|Does everyone contribute?|What they can. Time and willing hands count as much as grain.
